items.title: UKMTO updates Hormuz tanker warning: reported second strike, crew unaccounted for
items.summary: UKMTO's update to warning 208 reports a second strike on a tanker near Khasab, Oman, and says crew are currently unaccounted for, reversing an earlier safe-crew report. Reuters meanwhile reports recovering Middle East oil exports and stable early crude prices. Neither casualties nor a sustained cargo-flow loss have been independently verified.

observations.value: Update 001 timestamp 17 Nov 07:45 UTC; reported second strike; crew status unaccounted for; damage unknown

items.title: Red Cat plunges premarket after withdrawing full-year revenue target
items.summary: Red Cat withdrew its 2026 revenue target after slower contract funding and awards, despite reporting quarterly revenue growth. Premarket shares fell sharply. Cash holdings provide a buffer, but timing and conversion of defense procurement into funded revenue are uncertain.

observations.label: November 16 company results
observations.value: Q3 revenue $11.8M (+22% YoY); cash $242.7M; full-year 2026 revenue outlook withdrawn

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Procurement awards, customer deliveries, burn rate and inventory; funded contract conversion could improve outlook

items.key_finding: Revenue guidance withdrawal points to real execution and funding risk behind RCAT's premarket repricing.

items.title: Nvidia earnings to test AI-sector spending and margins amid leadership change
items.summary: Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close following a widespread AI-equity selloff and Jensen Huang's departure as CEO. Investors are examining data-center demand, margins, free cash generation and export restrictions. A modest premarket decline does not establish weaker chip shipments or orders.

items.title: Powell fiscal Q4 results show record electrical-infrastructure order backlog
items.summary: Powell Industries reported strong quarterly earnings, substantial order growth and major LNG and data-center project awards after the US close. The order book supports a real-world grid and power-equipment demand thesis despite the broader semiconductor selloff. Capacity execution, project margins and backlog conversion remain key risks; no reliable post-release stock move was verified.

items.title: Semiconductor index closes down five percent as AI selloff broadens
items.summary: Monday's US closing session confirmed a broad semiconductor rout: the PHLX semiconductor index fell 5%, with Micron, AMD, Intel, Marvell and Arm each down at least 6%. The Nasdaq lost 2.5% and S&P 500 lost 1.9%. Nvidia leadership uncertainty, tightening export policy and AI financing concerns contributed, but an industry-wide customer-demand collapse is unproven.

observations.label: November 16 US closing market
observations.value: SOX -5.0%; Nasdaq Composite -2.5%; S&P 500 -1.9%; Nvidia about -4%; AP/Barron's/MarketWatch

observations.label: Semiconductor breadth
observations.value: MU, AMD, INTC, MRVL and ARM each closed at least -6% (MarketWatch)

observations.label: Catalyst, risks and next checks
observations.value: Nvidia November 17 earnings and guidance, export restrictions, AI financing, confirmed order demand and sector breadth; firm end-demand data and broad stabilization would challenge the selloff narrative

items.key_finding: Confirmed close shows AI-linked selling has broadened into a material semiconductor-sector rout.
